title: Patient Recruitment FAQ: Solution, Funnel, Outreach, Sites and Go-Live

items.answer: ClairLabs runs an AI-enabled digital solution that takes participant recruitment end to end: identifying potential participants, qualifying them, and handing them over warm to trial sites. The scope ends once a participant clears site-specific evaluation and is officially selected and recruited.
items.escalation: For programme commercials or scope beyond recruitment, check with the programme lead rather than promising it from this material.
items.nuance: ClairLabs owns identification, qualification and warm handover - the site owns clinical evaluation, informed consent and selection.
items.question: What is the ClairLabs patient recruitment solution?

items.answer: Step 1 is primary digital screening: the participant completes an online screener and shares contact details with initial consent. Step 2 is platform onboarding, where qualified leads enter the centralized Patient Recruitment Platform for further qualification. Step 3 is secondary human screening, where RNN personnel connect with the participant to secure consent and run a detailed questionnaire. Step 4 is site referral and evaluation: qualified participants are referred to the nearest or preferred site for clinical evaluation and informed consent procedures. Step 5 is trial recruitment: participants who clear site-specific evaluations are officially selected and recruited, which ends ClairLabs responsibility.
items.escalation: If a participant disputes eligibility after referral, hand the case to the site team - do not re-adjudicate centrally.
items.nuance: Screening is two-tier by design: a digital tier for scale, then a human tier for consent quality and detail.
items.question: What are the steps of the recruitment journey?

items.answer: Six pillars: precise digital patient outreach, HCP outreach, data-driven outreach, patient advocacy groups, swift site alignment and go-live, and an enriched patient experience. Together they cover finding participants, working through clinicians and advocates, getting sites live fast, and keeping participants engaged.
items.escalation: Do not present the six pillars as a sequence - they run in parallel and reinforce each other.
items.nuance: Memorize all six: digital outreach, HCP outreach, data-driven outreach, advocacy groups, site alignment, patient experience.
items.question: What challenges does the approach address, and how?

items.answer: The funnel starts with a multichannel awareness ecosystem - Google, Meta and endemic health sites such as WebMD and Healthline, bought programmatically with audience segmentation to find even rare conditions. Top and mid-funnel activity (YouTube, programmatic display, educational content) builds high-intent consideration. Conversion capture and retention follows, and the bottom-funnel close uses lead forms, pre-screening tools and direct search ads. Because 70-90% of people do not convert on first touch, robust re-engagement and retargeting run throughout.

items.escalation: Media-mix choices and budgets sit with the campaign team - this course teaches the funnel logic, not the media plan.
items.nuance: The single most quotable number in the funnel: 70-90% initial non-conversion, which is why retargeting is structural, not optional.
items.question: How does the AI-driven recruitment funnel work?

items.answer: Three complementary motions. Digital affinity: NPI-targeted programmatic ads and geo-fencing around medical conferences. KOL-based influence: key opinion leaders advocate for trials and build credibility through peer networks, because physician-to-physician trust is the primary driver of credibility in medical outreach. Offline presence in high-affinity locations: clinics, centers of excellence, primary care, plus local clinics, libraries, coffee shops, stadiums and billboards. The offline and KOL motions matter most for complex or rare therapeutic areas.
items.escalation: KOL engagement must follow medical-compliance review - never promise KOL support for a specific site or trial from this material.
items.nuance: Match the motion to the disease: rare or complex conditions lean on KOL and offline presence; broad conditions lean on digital affinity.
items.question: How does HCP outreach work?

items.answer: Five sources feed identification: wearable app ecosystems (behavioral and physiological signals against health thresholds), digital therapeutics platform populations (verified, condition-specific users already managing chronic conditions), pharmacy network-triggered recruitment (near-real-time prescription data), EHR-triggered real-time trial alerts (matching algorithms embedded in electronic health records), and AI predictive recruitment that predicts clinical decision windows and triggers messaging when patients seek alternative treatments. The shift is from demographic-based outreach to behavioral and physiological identification.
items.escalation: All data use must stay within consent and privacy review - never describe a data source as approved for a specific trial without checking.
items.nuance: If asked for one line: reach patients during clinical decision windows, using real-time data, not demographics.
items.question: What data and intelligence strategies find participants?

items.answer: Patient advocacy groups bring trust that sponsors cannot buy, and their registries give access to hard-to-reach populations, including in rare-disease networks. AI-driven inclusion and exclusion matching filters registry patients precisely, and education-led conversion - patient ambassadors and webinars - reduces misinformation and supports both recruitment and retention. The combined effect is higher recruitment with far fewer screen failures.

items.escalation: Do not quote specific PAG contribution percentages externally - use the deck figures only inside training unless the numbers are re-verified.
items.nuance: Trust plus precision is the formula: PAG trust opens the door, AI matching and education carry the participant through it.
items.question: What role do patient advocacy groups and registries play?

items.answer: Rapid site activation streamlines the launch of high-performing sites to cut trial timelines. Hyper-localized outreach campaigns run in the immediate vicinity of trial sites, and real-time performance analytics with live data and rolling campaigns monitor recruitment health per site. Investigator engagement programmes build alignment through dedicated outreach, sites get standardized tools for immediate recruitment success, and locations are targeted on high patient density for better enrollment.

items.escalation: Site selection and activation decisions sit with operations - this course teaches the model, not the site list.
items.nuance: Site work is a loop, not a launch: activate, monitor live, engage investigators, optimize - continuously.
items.question: How are sites aligned and brought live?

items.answer: Five elements: comprehensive journey mapping that finds and fixes pain points from awareness to trial completion; real-time engagement platforms with consistent, active communication so nobody is lost to silence; concierge-level personalized care that is culturally sensitive and language-specific to the patient's disease stage; peer-driven community trust built on testimonials and peer experiences rather than clinical messaging; and continuous feedback loops that replace end-of-study surveys with real-time improvement. The architecture compresses site referral to minutes.
items.escalation: Personalization never overrides protocol - consent and eligibility language stay exactly as approved.
items.nuance: Minutes, not days: site referral speed is the headline proof that the architecture works.
items.question: What makes the participant experience patient-centric?

items.answer: Week 1 is content creation and review, week 2 is sponsor review with IRB-ready content submission. Week 3 covers internal preparation, testing and training, and the go-live event lands in week 4 - within 2 days of IRB changes. Week 6 is optimization: tuning non-performing ads and removing ad fatigability. The new process is markedly shorter than the old pattern of 4-week content plus 4-week go-live phases.
items.escalation: Timelines compress only if sponsor review and IRB inputs arrive on schedule - flag slippage early rather than absorbing it.
items.nuance: Anchor dates to remember: go-live in week 4 (within 2 days of IRB changes), optimization in week 6.
items.question: What is the accelerated go-live roadmap?

items.answer: Six: AI-driven patient identification powered by real-world-data ecosystems; 2-tier smart screening that pairs AI matching with RNN support to simplify complex eligibility questions for patients; next-gen omnichannel outreach with AI campaign optimization and advanced retargeting; site-aligned executional agility through synchronized activation and lean, fast decision cycles; patient experience-driven design with personalized communication and RNN retention support; and high-quality cost advantage from low overheads without sacrificing speed or compliance.
items.escalation: Differentiators describe the model - never turn them into guarantees for a specific trial in front of a sponsor.
items.nuance: If you remember one, remember 2-tier smart screening: AI plus a human layer that speaks plainly to patients.
items.question: What sets ClairLabs apart from the competition?

items.answer: Tier 1 is AI: matching algorithms identify precisely matched candidates from real-world-data ecosystems. Tier 2 is human: RNN personnel simplify complex eligibility questions for patients, secure consent and run the detailed questionnaire. Machines scale the search, people earn the trust.
items.escalation: RNN staff work from approved scripts - this course teaches the model, not the questionnaire wording.
items.nuance: Two tiers, two jobs: AI finds, RNN qualifies.
items.question: What is 2-tier smart screening?

items.answer: A hub-and-spoke model that enriches the patient experience, with dashboards giving trial-wide transparency that builds trust across stakeholders. The deck reports cases including 61% more patients delivered and a 12-month recruitment request delivered in 10 months.
items.escalation: Case numbers are deck figures for training - verify current figures with the programme team before quoting them to sponsors.
items.nuance: Transparency is itself a retention tool: dashboards keep every stakeholder aligned.
items.question: What proof backs the model?

items.answer: This course certifies the learner completed the patient recruitment induction: the end-to-end journey, the funnel, outreach motions, site activation, patient experience and the go-live roadmap. It carries a 12-question check with a 70% pass mark, and completion issues a certificate that says in brief what the course taught.
